title: Writer Automates Publishing Tasks with Claude Code for CMS
summary: Developer Alfred Lua shares how Claude Code automates CMS publishing workflows, letting writers focus on content creation instead of technical tasks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Developer Alfred Lua built an agentic CMS using Claude Code to handle repetitive publishing tasks automatically.
- The system automates image optimization, metadata generation, SEO formatting, and cross-platform distribution without manual intervention.
- Writers can now focus entirely on content creation while Claude Code manages technical publishing workflows end to end.


Developer and writer Alfred Lua has demonstrated a practical application of[Claude Code](https://emergent.sh/learn/claude-code-review) that addresses a common pain point for content creators: the technical overhead of publishing. By building what he calls an "agentic CMS," Lua uses Claude Code to automate repetitive publishing tasks, freeing writers to focus exclusively on content creation rather than technical implementation.


## How the Agentic CMS Works


Lua's system leverages Claude Code's ability to execute multi-step workflows autonomously. When a writer finishes a draft, Claude Code takes over the publishing pipeline. The AI agent handles image optimization and compression, generates alt text and metadata, formats content for SEO standards, and manages cross-platform distribution. Each task previously required manual intervention or custom scripts. Now the entire workflow runs automatically once triggered.


The implementation represents a shift from traditional content management systems that require writers to understand technical details. Instead of configuring image sizes, writing meta descriptions, or formatting HTML, writers simply write. Claude Code interprets publishing requirements and executes them without additional input.


## Officially Launched on November 20, 2026


Lua shared the agentic CMS project on November 20, 2026, through his personal site at alfredlua.com/agentic-cms. The post gained immediate traction on Hacker News, where developers and content creators discussed the implications for publishing workflows. The timing aligns with growing interest in AI agents that handle domain-specific tasks rather than general-purpose coding assistance.


## Technical Publishing Tasks Automated


The system automates several categories of work that typically slow down publishing cycles:


- Image processing: resizing, compression, format conversion, and responsive variant generation
- Metadata creation: title tags, meta descriptions, Open Graph tags, and schema markup
- Content formatting: heading hierarchy, internal linking, code block styling, and accessibility attributes
- Distribution coordination: scheduling, platform-specific formatting, and social media preview generation


Each automation reduces the time between finishing a draft and publishing by eliminating manual steps. Writers no longer context-switch between writing and technical configuration.


## Implications for Content Operations


Lua's implementation demonstrates how Claude Code can specialize in domain-specific workflows beyond software development. Publishing operations involve predictable, rule-based tasks that benefit from automation but previously required custom development. By using Claude Code as the automation engine, solo creators and small teams gain capabilities typically reserved for larger organizations with dedicated engineering resources.


The agentic CMS approach also suggests a template for other workflow automation projects. Any domain with repetitive technical tasks surrounding creative work could benefit from similar Claude Code implementations. The pattern applies to video production, podcast publishing, newsletter distribution, and other content-heavy operations.


## What This Means


Alfred Lua's agentic CMS shows Claude Code moving beyond code generation into operational automation for creative professionals. Writers gain time previously lost to publishing overhead, while technical quality remains consistent through automated enforcement of standards. The project provides a concrete example of AI agents handling end-to-end workflows in production environments, not just experimental demos. As more creators adopt similar patterns, the boundary between writing and publishing continues to blur, with AI handling the technical bridge between the two.
